arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The United States argues the compact creates a statutory duty to distribute water to Texas.
Texas and New Mexico argue the United States cannot raise compact claims in this matter.
Justice Sotomayor asked what specific federal interests the compact protects.
Justice Ginsburg asked how to distinguish when a party can sue under a compact.

paragraphs: The United States argues the Rio Grande Compact creates a statutory duty to deliver water to Texas. Texas and New Mexico argue the federal government lacks standing to raise these claims.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the federal government's role in interstate water disputes. It clarifies whether the United States can sue to enforce compact duties. The outcome shapes future water rights litigation between states and the federal government.
